1d3f70b3363b8fba: JOHOR BARU, Sept 26 — The sun was merciless, the street was packed, and nobody was going anywhere.
Tamannaah Bhatia was coming to town, and Johor was ready.

The Bollywood and Kollywood star was in Johor Baru to officiate the launch of Yazhini Gold & Diamonds’ new Ayra & Abhinaya Diamond Collections at its Jalan Segget store, at an event hosted by television personality Kiki Vijay.

Her fans were there long before she was. By 10am, the street was already filling up with admirers armed with posters, umbrellas and phones on full charge, staking out their spots as the midday heat climbed. By early afternoon, hundreds had squeezed along Jalan Segget, craning their necks towards the entrance at every passing car.
At 2.50pm, the moment finally arrived.
Tamannaah stepped out in a pink saree and the street exploded. Screams of “Tamannaah! Tamannaah!” drowned out the traffic as a forest of phones shot into the air.

She did not just wave and disappear. The actress made her way along the barricades, stopping for selfies, grabbing outstretched hands and trading a few words with fans who had been baking in the heat since morning.
“I am so happy to see everyone still here and in such high energy despite this afternoon heat,” she said, beaming at the crowd.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Indian actress Tamannaah Bhatia smiles and waves to fans as she arrives at Yazhini Gold & Diamonds in Jalan Segget, Johor Baru.
For a star who had touched down from Mumbai only the night before, she seemed genuinely taken aback by the reception.
“Johor fans are beautiful people. From the time I arrived last night, I have been treated with so much love,” she said.
That warmth, she added, did not stop at the barricades.
“Just like the hospitality I received from Malaysians, the sales team here gave me the same warm welcome. Wherever you go, a store’s sales team are the most important people,” she said.
Yazhini Gold & Diamonds marketing manager Velan said the brand already had its sights set further north.
“Kuala Lumpur is part of our future expansion plans. More details will be announced soon,” he said.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Yazhini Gold & Diamonds owner Hemaananthan Thayalam, television host Kiki Vijay, actress Tamannaah Bhatia and manager Karthikeyan pose for a photo at the launch of the Ayra & Abhinaya Diamond Collections in Johor Baru.

The visit capped a big week for the actress. Just a day earlier, her new Hindi fantasy thriller The Vvaan: Force of the Forrest, in which she stars opposite Sidharth Malhotra, opened in cinemas. The film is steeped in Bihari culture and folklore, and Tamannaah wore that pride on her sleeve.
“India as a country has so much culture, and in this film we showed our culture. It is very exciting to celebrate it with all of you here, who also have so much respect for Indian culture,” she said.
And before she left, she made sure the crowd went home happy, blowing kisses from the stage.
“Big love, big kisses. Thank you for all your support always, and thank you for being here today. Love you guys,” she said.
Tamannaah made her acting debut in 2005 and has since become one of South Indian cinema’s biggest names.
Tamil audiences fell for her in hits such as Kalloori, Ayan opposite Suriya, Paiyaa and Siruthai opposite Karthi, Veeram opposite Ajith Kumar, and more recently the horror-comedy Aranmanai 4.
Her dance number Kaavaalaa from the Rajinikanth blockbuster Jailer set dance floors on fire, while the Baahubali franchise made her a household name far beyond India.
586b101d1d050e06: BAKU: George Russell held off Red Bull's four-times world champion Max Verstappen to complete a lights-to-flag win in Saturday's Azerbaijan Grand Prix for Mercedes with teammate Kimi Antonelli limiting the damage to his championship lead by finishing fifth.

Russell took the flag 0.196 seconds ahead of the flying Dutchman, who started eighth but crossed the line nearly side-by-side with his Mercedes rival after two safety car phases turned a cruise into a fight for survival for the Briton.
Frenchman Isack Hadjar, who was handed a contract extension by Red Bull earlier this week and missed the last three races with a wrist injury, completed the podium on his racing return.
The win around the Baku street track was the eighth of Russell's career, third of the season and his first since the Austrian Grand Prix at the end of June.

"It's amazing to be back on the top step of the podium," said Russell. "Every race since the (summer) break I've gone from strength to strength and I feel more like myself again."

His drive on Saturday was less like his Monza charge – where he went from 19th to first – and more a slow burn recovery.
Charles Leclerc took fourth for Ferrari ahead of the 20-year-old Italian. His seven-times world champion teammate Lewis Hamilton was sixth.

Carlos Sainz rounded out the top 10 for Williams. - Reuters
0df343ab82b2059b: PETALING JAYA: A resident of Pangsapuri Saujana in Damansara Damai was left shaken after a storm struck the area yesterday, damaging his car when a tree branch fell on it.
"My ears were ringing from the sound of the extremely strong winds, followed by thunder. I was too afraid to leave my home," said Mazlan Ismail, 59.
He said the incident occurred at about 1pm, after the weather had initially been calm before the sky suddenly darkened and strong winds swept through the area.

As soon as the storm subsided, he rushed to the parking area and found his car's windows shattered, while the roof and sides of the rear boot were badly dented after being struck by the fallen branch.
"This is the second time in 3 years that we have experienced a storm this strong," he said when met at the scene.
The situation was reportedly worse in nearby areas, particularly at Pangsapuri Impian, where several residents' vehicles were damaged by fallen trees.
Residents also raised concerns over what they claimed was a lack of regular maintenance of trees along roadsides.
Pangsapuri Suria resident Rafizan Ramli, 40, said the large trees in the densely populated residential area had not been properly maintained.
"Most of the trees along the roadside have grown too large and dense, while some appear to be in poor condition.
"There has been no regular maintenance. When a strong storm hits, this is what happens.
"We urge the authorities to learn from this incident and immediately trim trees that pose a risk before someone loses their life," he said.
Rafizan said fallen trees also blocked several major roads, causing severe traffic congestion.

"Help took some time to arrive as responders had to find routes that were still accessible. However, we are grateful that the Civil Defence Force, the Fire and Rescue Department and local authorities acted quickly," he said.
Checks at the scene found that tree-cutting and debris-clearing operations were still underway to clear affected roads and ease traffic congestion.

904b2b6dae9944c5: PETALING JAYA: UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd sudah mempunyai pelan pemulihan bagi menangani kedudukan kewangannya susulan kerugian terkumpul kira-kira RM157 juta.

“Jika UiTM Holdings kukuh, nilai akhirnya kembali kepada UiTM. Jika ia terus lemah, UiTM juga menerima kesannya,” katanya.
Tambahnya, pelan pemulihan telah tersedia dan apa yang diperlukan kini ialah penyelarasan, keputusan serta pelaksanaan di seluruh ekosistem UiTM.
6f466ad3da857390: NAGOYA: After 44 years, Malaysia will have a representative in the men's 200m final at the Asian Games after young sprinter Danish Iftikhar Roslee achieved a historic feat in Nagoya today.

f3297fbb310281d9: LONDON, Sept 26 — Mystery has engulfed the fate of legendary British adventurer Ranulph Fiennes, after relatives and friends went public claiming he was missing and his wife was isolating him — with one reportedly even asking King Charles for help.

Fiennes, the first person to cross the Earth pole to pole in the early 1980s, was last seen publicly nearly two years ago, months after opening up about a Parkinson’s diagnosis he received years earlier.
Last week, the Daily Telegraph reported the 82-year-old had been placed in a succession of care homes by his wife, Louise Millington-Cotes, who has allegedly put strict conditions on his care.

In a follow-up Friday in its months-long probe, the newspaper said a care sector watchdog in Wales had concluded he was “unlawfully deprived of his liberty” when housed at a facility there earlier this year.
Meanwhile, Fiennes’s stepson, Alex Millington-Cotes, this week launched a crowdfunding campaign for legal fees to “locate and safeguard” him.
“You may have recently heard the deeply concerning news: Sir Ranulph Fiennes is missing,” he wrote online, adding he had “tried multiple avenues to find” him.
Calling Fiennes “a national treasure”, he described his stepfather as “a man of immense heart, kindness, and selflessness”.
Swiss-based ex-explorer and Fiennes collaborator Michael Kobold has joined the campaign to “help lift the veil of secrecy” around his whereabouts.

“My friend of almost 30 years has gone missing and nobody besides a tiny handful of individuals seems to want to do anything to change this disgraceful status quo,” he wrote in a lengthy blogpost this month.
‘Not well’
Fiennes has long been a towering figure in exploration, acclaimed by the Guinness Book of World Records as the “greatest living explorer”.
His epic 1979-1982 Transglobe Expedition saw him proclaimed the first person to visit both north and south poles by surface means.
He later became the first to cross Antarctica completely on foot and also ran seven marathons on seven continents within a week.
Hailing from one of the most storied families in England — which counts actors Joseph and Ralph Fiennes among its extended ranks — he has been friends with King Charles for decades.
His 34-year marriage to first wife Virginia ended with her death in 2004, and he wed Millington-Cotes the following year. The couple have a daughter and stepson.

In his last public appearance — a pre-recorded video played at an October 2024 Royal Geographic Society event — he read from an off-screen script apologising for not being “well enough” to attend, The Telegraph said.
The daily reports Millington-Cotes was granted lasting power of attorney that year and has become his legal guardian, placing Fiennes in care homes in London, Wales and then northwest England.
It claims she has refused to allow some friends to visit, while also insisting any visitors sign non-disclosure agreements (NDAs).
‘King ‘concerned’
Arabella McIntyre-Brown, Fiennes’s former sister-in-law, last year checked herself into the London care home where he was living and made contact.
“He was lucid — personality intact, memory clear,” she told The Telegraph, adding he had stressed he wanted to see his friends.
However, after the visit Fiennes was moved and later placed in a Welsh home, according to the newspaper.
“It’s absurd,” McIntyre-Brown told the Telegraph. “It’s like we’d stumbled into a John Le Carre novel.”
The Welsh care-home owner told the paper Millington-Cotes had failed to provide the legally required paperwork designed to protect vulnerable adults, so sought advice from the industry’s regulator.
The Care Inspectorate of Wales responded in January that Fiennes was “being deprived of his liberty unlawfully” without the paperwork, it reported.
The Inspectorate told AFP “it would not be appropriate” to comment.
Meanwhile an old friend of Fiennes, Anton Bowring, claims he had contact with Buckingham Palace last year, when a staffer told him “the king was concerned for Fiennes”, the Telegraph said.
Buckingham Palace declined to comment to AFP. Millington-Cotes could not be reached for comment.
“It’s the extraordinary final chapter in a remarkable life,” Bowring told The Telegraph.
“I know he’s still out there, alive. But I’ve grieved for him. I’ve said goodbye.” — AFP
27d645f9fb270530: JAKARTA, Sept 26 — Wildfires that tore through Indonesian Borneo’s vast tropical forests have piled pressure on critically endangered Bornean orangutans, the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) said Saturday.
Indonesia has been battling fires for weeks in parts of Borneo and Sumatra, sending suffocating haze across the islands and neighbouring Malaysia and Singapore.
Fires are currently burning within habitats containing 52 per cent of Borneo’s orangutan population, including 13 of the 20 largest remaining populations, it said.
“Fire and smoke exposure impose measurable physiological, behavioural and ecological costs on orangutans in peat forest habitats,” the conservation network said.
During haze, orangutans show signs of fat breakdown despite eating more and resting more, suggesting elevated energy demands likely from an immune system forced to work harder, it said.
Wildfires have also been reported in the habitats of five gibbon species across Sumatra and Borneo, the conservation network said.

“Gibbons breathe the same smoke-laden air as the people living alongside them, and there is every reason to expect they suffer similar respiratory harm, on top of habitat loss and disruption to the behaviours that keep wild populations viable.”
As of Tuesday, Indonesia had rescued 100 animals, including 53 orangutans, that were threatened by the blazes, a forestry ministry spokesman said.
Conservationists call on the authorities to go beyond first response and implement prevention measures.
“Emergency response must be followed by sustained investment in preventing future fires,” Ronna Saab of Forum Konservasi Orangutan Indonesia (Forina) said in a statement.

Those measures include “protecting and rewetting peatlands, addressing drainage and deforestation, and ensuring burned forests are protected from subsequent conversion and appropriately restored,” Ronna said.
The Indonesian government said more than 202,000 hectares of land were burnt countrywide between January and July, the latest available data.
The Nusantara Atlas project has put the number at closer to 900,000 hectares between January and August. — Bernama
fdf5613482d76925: MILAN, Sept 26 — Gucci designer Demna presented his first truly “personal” show at Milan Fashion Week yesterday, hoping to revitalise the storied Italian brand with a glamorous, eccentric and rebellious style.
Demna’s men are hooded bad boys, wearing tartan-lined jackets or suits with pronounced shoulders, cropped trousers that expose the ankle, and triple-buckle belts for a rock-and-roll touch.

The women evoke Milanese style from the 1980s with a hint of eccentricity: classic black suits revealing the midriff, leather coats worn with a scarf or enormous furs, all perched on high-heeled boots.
Some sport a more punk look, with chains around their necks.
Demna wrote on Instagram before the show that the collection represented “my complete personal vision for the brand” after one year studying it.
“Gucci stands for being rooted in the idea of belonging to a more glamourous world and in the audacity to remake that world in your own image,” he wrote.
For the 45-year-old Georgian designer, whose full name is Demna Gvasalia, Gucci is “luxury that wants to be seen”, with “eccentricity, danger or sex appeal” lurking behind its more bourgeois roots.

Sales at the flagship label of the Kering group — which also includes Saint Laurent, Bottega Veneta and Balenciaga — have disappointed in recent years, after several boom years under the creative direction of Alessandro Michele.

Since the former Balenciaga designer’s arrival at Gucci in 2025 and the presentation of two first collections in February and May that took inspiration from the brand’s archives, sales continued to decline in the second quarter.
But they declined at a slower rate than in the first, Kering said in July.
Party in LA
On Thursday night, Roberto Cavalli turned to Los Angeles for inspiration, tapping exuberant, festive California excess for the brand’s Spring/Summer 2027 collection.

With leopard prints, feathers, billowy kimonos and imprinted red leather, designer Fausto Puglisi channelled an over-the-top LA party at a runway show attended by rapper Cardi B, tennis player Naomi Osaka and Italian influencer Chiara Ferragni.
A zebra-print kimono was paired with kaleidoscopic printed jeans barely covering a zebra-print thong.
A burst of feathers emerged from the hip of an embroidered jeans miniskirt, with a slinky button-down leopard shirt on top.
“I’m trying to respond to a terrible time” around the world, Fausto Puglisi told AFP after the show.
The Sicilian designer said he was trying to “resist by creating something beautiful that brings optimism, conceived as a setting for a director or a writer”.
The result: lace-up tops baring the midriff, a tunic with a cheetah head and flowers woven onto the lower legs of jeans.
In show notes, the brand said the collection was meant to evoke “feverishly constructed chaos that seems alive,” adding that Cavalli was “party, escapism, joy”.
It was Puglisi’s first show since Roberto Cavalli was taken over by US group Marquee Brands, owner of Ben Sherman and BCBGMAXAZRIA.
Also Thursday, Emporio Armani showed the last mixed collection designed by Leo dell’Orco and Silvana Armani, ahead of the arrival of Dario Vitale, announced earlier this month.

33fc23da63e90e0e: From Azam Mohd

Negeri Sembilan’s royal dispute is ultimately a test of constitutional method, not loyalty. Labels such as “derhaka” or “coup” may mobilise supporters, but they cannot substitute for proving jurisdiction, procedure, and evidence.

The state constitution gives the undangs a distinctive role. The Attorney-General’s Chambers acknowledged on Sept 17 that the chieftains possess power concerning a Yang Dipertuan Besar’s removal, but said Article 10 imposes mandatory grounds and procedures.

It found no evidence establishing the specified disqualification grounds and regarded the April 19 proclamation as invalid. The opposing Secretariat of the Undang Yang Empat subsequently maintained that preliminary and further inquiries occurred on March 5 and April 19.

What is clearer is what the executive cannot do. The AGC stated that the menteri besar and executive council possess no unilateral authority to terminate or vacate the ruler’s office. The Dewan Keadilan dan Undang likewise says Article XVI places questions of Malay custom, including appointment and removal, within the Dewan’s jurisdiction.

The menteri besar’s signature presents a narrower question. Umno’s published position says Article 10(2) makes the signature part of implementing an undang's decision, not the source of removal power. Yet whether a signature can validate an instrument depends first on satisfaction of the preceding constitutional requirements.
Ismail Lasim also alleged that an earlier signature was obtained under duress and lodged a police report. That allegation is evidence for investigation, not proof of criminal liability.

Judicial orders add another layer. On June 5, the Seremban High Court granted an ad interim injunction maintaining the existing composition of the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang and its secretary pending jurisdictional and justiciability questions or further order.

On July 8, the court granted leave for contempt proceedings against six individuals over an alleged breach; the Court of Appeal later stayed those contempt proceedings. Leave establishes a prima facie basis to proceed, not guilt.
Article XVI’s finality language concerning adat does not automatically erase judicial supervision over every procedural question.
Malaysian constitutionalism generally distinguishes the merits of an entrusted decision from whether the correct authority acted within constitutional limits.

Article 71 guarantees state constitutions and provides federal mechanisms in specified circumstances; Article 181 preserves rulers’ sovereignty subject to the Federal Constitution. Neither provision creates an ordinary shortcut for replacing Negeri Sembilan’s constitutional machinery. An emergency under Article 150 requires the constitutional conditions for a proclamation; controversy alone is insufficient.
Likewise, sedition, treason, offences against parliamentary democracy, arrest or disqualification require their own statutory elements and evidence. None follows automatically from disagreement.

The consequences nevertheless extend beyond Seremban. Melaka’s assembly was dissolved effective Sept 23, and its election must follow within 60 days. Barisan Nasional, Pakatan Harapan and Perikatan Nasional have incentives to frame Negeri Sembilan around loyalty, stability, and constitutional respect.

But there is insufficient evidence to conclude that the dispute will determine Melaka voting behaviour. Royal sentiment may influence some voters; household economics, candidates, turnout and coalition arrangements remain competing mechanisms.
For Umno and BN, the strategic danger is allowing legal ambiguity to become an identity test.
For PH and PN, exploiting unresolved proceedings as settled wrongdoing carries the same institutional risk.
The unity government’s interest should be narrower: preserve legal process, avoid executive improvisation, and ensure enforcement agencies act independently.

The evidence points to a dispute that remains legally conditional, not politically settled: Article 10 may empower the undang to remove the Yang Dipertuan Besar, but only if its mandatory grounds and procedures are satisfied; the menteri besar and executive council have no established unilateral power to do so; the validity of the April 19 proclamation remains contested; and any alleged breach of the High Court’s injunction is still for judicial determination.
Claims that criminal offences, disqualification, or federal intervention automatically follow are therefore premature, because each requires separate legal elements and proof.
That is why constitutional restraint, rather than partisan certainty, should define the response of every institution.

The responsible path is institutional restraint: preserve records, publish legally permissible reasons, obey subsisting court orders and let competent courts determine reviewable procedural questions while constitutionally designated adat bodies decide matters entrusted to them.
Negeri Sembilan does not need actors to manufacture a winner. It needs every institution to prove that constitutional authority still means authority exercised according to law.
Azam Mohd is an FMT reader.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.

35a5a95225563043: BEIJING: China "respects" Washington's switch in phrasing from artificial intelligence to "super intelligence", the foreign ministry said on Saturday, after Donald Trump said Xi Jinping appeared to like the rewording.
The US president announced on Tuesday that his administration would rename AI as "super intelligence", or SI, in official communications.
The technology was high on the agenda during the summit between the US and Chinese leaders in Washington this week.

"Like almost everyone else, (Xi) seemed to like calling the poorly and inaccurately named Artificial Intelligence to a far more accurate and important name, SUPER INTELLIGENCE," Trump wrote on his social media platform after talks with Xi.
China has not explicitly confirmed or denied Trump's characterisation of the discussion.
However, Beijing's foreign ministry said on Saturday it "attaches importance" to Trump's adoption of the term.
"Regarding the artificial intelligence phrasing question, the Chinese side attaches importance to the US side's position and respects the US side's wording," the ministry said in a statement.

"Artificial intelligence technologies are continuously developing, all parties can strengthen exchanges, discuss in-depth and seek consensus in light of the latest situation," said the statement from an unidentified ministry spokesman said.
China and the US agreed to set up a "communication channel" for AI incidents, both sides said after the summit.
Billionaire Trump has repeatedly dismissed fears that AI could pose a threat to humanity, although Xi has taken a more measured tone and said the technology must develop under human control.
f9630aec833d855c: NAGOYA: South Korea gatecrashed Japan's party to win the women's basketball gold at the Asian Games on Saturday, surviving a huge late scare to beat the hosts 75-70 in the final.
Japan were looking to win the title for the first time since 1998 and they were backed by a noisy crowd at the 17,000-capacity Aichi International Arena in Nagoya.
But the Koreans took control of the game early and then held on in the fourth quarter as Japan launched a frantic fightback that fell just short.
It was South Korea's fourth Asian Games title and their first since 2014.
Lee Hae-ran was South Korea's top scorer with 24 points, followed by Kang Lee-seul with 21.
Japan were led by Haru Owaki with 23 points.
South Korea dominated in the first quarter, building a 15-3 lead to set the tone.
The Koreans looked comfortable until Japan finished the third quarter strongly and hit a three-pointer right at the buzzer.
Japan closed the gap further in the fourth quarter to threaten a remarkable comeback, but South Korea weathered the storm.
Every player in South Korea's squad also featured at the Women's World Cup in Germany earlier this month, where they lost to the hosts in the first knockout round.
Japan were also eliminated at the same stage at the World Cup but they brought an entirely different squad to the Asian Games.
China won the bronze medal, beating Taiwan 77-64.
Seven-time Asian Games champions China, featuring 223cm teenager Zhang Ziyu, lost to South Korea in the semi-finals. - AFP
7d85ca73a08afdd5: LONDON: Former Manchester City chairman David Bernstein said the club could face potentially "drastic" sanctions after reportedly being found guilty on all but one of 115 charges for breaching Premier League financial rules.
No official announcement has been made by the Premier League over the case and there is no indication of any possible punishment.
Abu Dhabi-backed City have always strenuously denied the charges and a club spokesman said the position had not changed.
It is understood City will appeal should the charges be upheld.

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence," the spokesman said.
City were charged by the Premier League in 2023 following an investigation into alleged breaches of rules between 2009 and 2018.
The club were accused of failing to provide accurate financial information and details of payments to players and coaches, as well as breaches of financial sustainability rules.
They were also charged with failing to cooperate with an investigation.
A hearing by an independent commission started in September 2024.
'Severe penalty'
Bernstein, who was City chairman between 1998 and 2003, told Times Radio that "money is not sufficient" in terms of a potential punishment, urging a swift appeal process.
"The appeal process cannot go on for year after year, I think that would be a disaster," he said. "Not just for this particular case but for English football generally. The timing is crucial.
"I can't give a view on the punishment. If they are found, after the appeal, guilty of (the) charges, my beloved club is going to face a very severe penalty.
"All I would say is that money is not sufficient, it would have to be something, unfortunately, more drastic than that," he said.
Oasis star and City fan Noel Gallagher described his "shock" at the developments.
Speaking on the Let Me Talk podcast, he said: "Surprised because only that the club have assured us all along that they vehemently denied any of these charges.
"So it was a bit of a shock to find out that we've been found guilty of all but one. But really overall just quite sad really. Sad for the fans and for the players," he said.
UK culture secretary Lisa Nandy described the case as "unsettling" for football fans and called for a swift resolution.
In 2020, Uefa imposed a two-year European ban on City as well as a fine for breaking financial fair-play rules, though that ban was later overturned by the Court of Arbitration for Sport.
If the reported guilty verdicts are confirmed, sanctions could include a severe points deduction and possibly even expulsion from the Premier League.
Everton and Nottingham Forest were both hit by points deductions in the 2023/2024 season for single breaches of profit and sustainability rules.
Other Premier League clubs are understood to be taking legal advice about compensation relating to the charges.
Under the ownership of Sheikh Mansour, whose Abu Dhabi United Group acquired the club in 2008, City have become the dominant force in English football.
They have won eight Premier League titles, a Champions League crown and multiple other trophies over the past 15 years.
The latest developments in the case come just months after former City manager Pep Guardiola left the club following a golden decade in charge at the Etihad.
Guardiola always backed the club's stance on the charges but threatened to walk away if he felt he had been lied to and they were proven to be true.

cfff068575906848: BANGKOK, Sept 26 — Malaysians in Bangkok have been urged to exercise caution and remain vigilant as persistent heavy rain and flooding continue to disrupt roads and daily activities across the Thai capital, with all 50 districts declared disaster zones.

In an advisory issued Saturday, the Malaysian Embassy in Bangkok urged Malaysians residing in or travelling to the city to keep abreast of the latest weather, road, and traffic conditions and plan their journeys in advance.

“Malaysians are advised to check road and flood conditions before travelling, allow additional travel time, avoid flood-affected areas, and consider alternative routes or modes of transport where necessary,” it said.

The embassy cautioned that weather and road conditions could change rapidly, particularly in flood-affected areas, and urged Malaysians to monitor local conditions and follow advisories and instructions issued by the relevant Thai authorities.

It said the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) provides an online Road Flood Monitoring System that allows the public to check road conditions and water levels at monitoring points across the capital.
The embassy said Malaysians could also report flooding or standing water through Traffy Fondue or contact the BMA Hotline at 1555, which operates around the clock.
For travel information, assistance or enquiries, Malaysians may contact the Tourism Authority of Thailand (TAT) Contact Centre at 1672 or the Tourist Police at 1155.
Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt earlier declared all 50 districts in the capital disaster zones, following persistent heavy rain that caused flooding and traffic disruptions.
Flooding was reported in 93 districts, 350 sub-districts, and 1,425 villages, while waterlogging affected 44 road locations in Bangkok.
As of 7am on Saturday, flooding remained in 21 provinces nationwide, affecting 27,109 households and 84,605 people, according to the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation (DDPM).
At press time, no casualties had been reported in Bangkok, although some e-hailing services had stopped accepting bookings due to road closures, while some shops remained closed. — Bernama
4ed7fd3421398df4: KOTA KINABALU: A special committee should be established under the technical committee of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) implementation action council to study the proposal to increase Sabah and Sarawak’s representation in Parliament.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department for Sabah and Sarawak affairs Mustapha Sakmud said the study would also determine a timeline for implementation of the proposal.

Mustapha said the special committee should comprise representatives from the Election Commission (EC), the legal affairs division, and the Sabah and Sarawak affairs division of the Prime Minister's Department, as well as the state governments.

“We hope that through this approach, we will be able to set out a clear timeline for increasing the number of parliamentary seats in Sabah and Sarawak,” he told reporters after launching a book at the Sabah International Convention Centre here today.

In a statement on Tuesday, Mustapha had said the Sabah and Sarawak affairs division had initiated discussions with the EC on the direction and implementation mechanism for the proposal to increase the number of MPs from Sabah and Sarawak.
He said discussions with the EC were still at an early stage, focussing on the methods and studies required to increase the number of parliamentary seats in the two states.

“Following the meeting, the EC informed us that it has specific methods in place. However, a detailed study is required because any increase in parliamentary seats in Borneo must take into account the corresponding increase in seats in the peninsula,” he said.

On Sept 11, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said the government had agreed to increase the proportion of parliamentary representation for Sabah and Sarawak from the current level, in line with the spirit of MA63.
ed87a6be23f0bb99: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Sept 26 — The Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority (Fama) has taken proactive steps to safeguard the nation’s food supply by establishing a special committee two months ago to prepare for the possible impact of El Nino.

Its chairman, Abang Ahmad Kerdee Abang Masagus, said the move reflected Fama’s early action to prepare for the phenomenon, including plans to procure and store agro-food products at Fama warehouses nationwide.
“At Fama, we established a committee two months ago. Although El Niño is an annual phenomenon, we took proactive measures this year instead of waiting for it to occur.

“By taking early action and coordinating with the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) on when the phenomenon is expected to begin, we were able to make early preparations this year,” he told reporters here today.

He said this when met at the Penang 2026 JAM Mega programme at Lotus’s Seberang Jaya, which was officiated by Penang State Rural Development, Agrotechnology, Food Security and Entrepreneurship Committee chairman Datuk Rashidi Zinol.

Previously, MetMalaysia director-general Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip was reported as saying that there was more than a 90 per cent probability of El Niño reaching the “very strong” or “Super El Nino” category between October and December.

Abang Ahmad Kerdee said Fama also planned to purchase selected agro-food products and keep them in its warehouses as buffer stocks against potential supply disruptions, including those caused by import and export issues.
He said Fama had warehouses in every state, including cold storage facilities, which would be fully utilised to ensure sufficient food supplies.
“The stocks include around 34 types of agro-food products, including red chillies, green chillies, cabbage and onions, as well as other food products such as chicken and beef.
“Should there be any issues, such as difficulties in securing imports or exports, we have a backup plan to ensure that there is sufficient supply of these products for several months,” he said.
Abang Ahmad Kerdee said the approach drew on the country’s experience during the Covid-19 pandemic, when early planning and adequate food stocks helped maintain continuity in food supplies. — Bernama

ff29fb8180736fa1: MUMBAI, Sept 26 — Drought has hit three-quarters of India’s richest state of Maharashtra, the government said today, after prolonged low rainfall in the region home to the megacity of Mumbai.
The declaration in Maharashtra came after the national weather department forecast India would end its annual monsoon season with a rainfall deficit, threatening farmers’ livelihoods.
A stronger-than-usual El Nino climate phenomenon, which typically brings drier conditions to South Asia, has also led to abnormal rain patterns, the weather department has said.
The government of Maharashtra, a huge western state whose capital Mumbai is India’s financial and commercial centre, said drought was present across 74 percent of the territory.
Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said the administration stood “firmly behind our farmer brethren” during the crisis.
The government will assess crop damage and “ensure that farmers, farm labourers and rural families receive the necessary assistance in a timely manner”, his office said.
Hundreds of millions of people in India depend on the June-to-September monsoon to bring vital rains that sustain agriculture and industry.
Maharashtra has a population of 130 million and is a major agricultural state that produces cotton, soybeans, sugarcane and pulses.
Many farmers depend on rain for irrigation and are highly vulnerable to crop failures, which can push whole families into financial crisis.
The impact of low rainfall is also being felt in southern India, where Karnataka state has also announced aid for farmers in drought-hit areas.
El Nino is a naturally occurring climate pattern associated with warmer ocean temperatures in the Pacific that can change wind and rainfall patterns around the world.
Scientists say human-caused climate change can amplify its effects by making more energy and moisture available to fuel extreme weather. — AFP
463678d2cc1ff49a: PARIS, Sept 26 — Pope Leo XIV was today to celebrate an open-air mass for hundreds of thousands of believers on the Champs Elysees in Paris, after saying it was possible to “live together in dignity and peace”.

The leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics was on a four-day trip to France, a secular country with deep Catholic roots, with his trip stirring enthusiasm and spiritual fervour among the faithful.

Parents arrived with pushchairs or children perched on their shoulders as crowds gathered in central Paris to catch a glimpse of the pontiff on the second day of the first official papal visit to France in nearly two decades.
The pope, 71, was due to lead the faithful in prayer from 3:00 pm (1300 GMT) at Place de la Concorde and along the adjoining Champs-Elysees.

On streets surrounding the Champs-Elysees, dozens of coaches dropped worshippers who had travelled from across France, many holding stools or folding chairs as they settled in for a wait of several hours.
Sylvie Leclerc, a 51-year-old teacher, clutched the Normandy flag.
“It’s a big event, we’ve come to share the Christian fervour,” she said.
“You don’t hear much from us Catholics, but now we’re going to make some noise! But to proclaim love, peace, joy,” she added.
‘Civilisation of love’
Fifteen-year-old Alix was among teenagers looking forward to the mass.
“We’re so lucky to be here,” she said, wearing electric blue mascara and glittery cross-shaped earrings.
“Seeing the pope is really something. After all, he’s God’s representative on Earth.”

The first US pontiff was visiting France seven months before voters choose a successor to centrist President Emmanuel Macron, with the anti-immigration far right eyeing its best opportunity yet to capture the presidency.
Macron will not attend the mass, but presidential hopefuls including far-right leader Marine Le Pen and centrist Edouard Philippe have confirmed their attendance.
Earlier in the day, the pope met migrants as he visited Maison Bakhita, an association supporting refugees.
He said it was “possible to encounter one another and to live together in dignity and peace.”
Dressed in a white cassock, Leo also stressed the “fundamental role of women in building a civilisation of love.”
The association said the pope’s visit sent a “message” ahead of the election.
‘Saints of France’
On Friday, an estimated 300,000 people turned out to see the pontiff as he waved from his popemobile on the way to the Notre Dame Cathedral.
“There is a sense of fervour reminiscent of that experienced over 40 years ago with John Paul II,” Francois Mabille, director of the Geopolitical Observatory on Religion, told broadcaster RMC.
On Friday, Pope Leo stressed the need for ethics to avoid an AI-driven “paradise of machines” and, as war rages in Ukraine for a fifth year, urged France to remain a “tireless champion of peace”.
He also told young adults at a stadium outside the French capital on Friday night that they were the “saints of France.”
In a deeply secular country, only around five percent of France’s 69 million residents go to Catholic church services regularly, a survey found last year.
But while infant baptisms have declined in recent years, increasing numbers of teenagers and adults are being baptised.
After the mass in Paris, Pope Leo will head to Lourdes, a town in southwestern France where, according to Catholic tradition, the Virgin Mary appeared in a grotto in 1858 to a peasant girl.
In Lourdes on Sunday, he will speak with seven victims of clerical sex abuse.
A 2021 inquiry found that clergy or lay members of the Church had abused about 330,000 people as minors in France, over seven decades.
In recent years, further accusations have emerged against charity icon Abbe Pierre and workers at a Catholic boarding school near Lourdes.
For the last leg of his trip, in Metz on Monday, Leo is expected to deliver a speech about peace in Europe. — AFP
5a0246e5e5f5c7c8: TEHRAN, Sept 26 — Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Tehran’s new plan to reopen the strategic Strait of Hormuz was coordinated with supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei, state media reported today, quoting an interview with US media.
Pezeshkian also told broadcaster CBS that the Islamic republic would fulfil its obligations were the United States to agree to the proposal, according to excerpts released by state news agency IRNA.
The strait is crucial for the world’s oil supply and central to the conflict between the US and Iran, which remains deadlocked after nearly seven months.
“Coordination with the leader of the revolution (the supreme leader)… has been carried out,” Pezeshkian said.
“If the US accepts it and fulfils its obligations, we will do the same, and there will be no issue in this regard,” he added.
Pezeshkian said that a six-member team in Iran has been meeting for discussions and has “the authority to make decisions”.
This team includes representatives from “various organisations and bodies, including the military, the parliament and the government”.
Washington has yet to publicly respond to Iran’s proposal but reports indicated that President Donald Trump had rejected the plan, which calls for a cessation of all hostilities in the Middle East.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said the plan’s conditions were the same as those laid out in a memorandum of understanding signed with the US in June.

37c0747d791a5325: ATHENS, Sept 26 — The bodies of an American couple visiting Greece were pulled today from an Athens building that collapsed following an explosion, officials said.

Four other people were missing, including an elderly British man and a Greek woman who shared an apartment, following the blast that occurred early Friday in Athens’s historic Plaka district, just below the Acropolis.
A rescue operation was ongoing, with AFP seeing mechanical diggers moving debris and thermal-imaging cameras being deployed.
The US woman and man had been staying in an apartment rented to tourists located on the floor above street level in the building, Greek rescue officials told journalists.
Authorities did not immediately release their identities.
The explosion that brought down the small, two-storey building was likely caused by a gas leak, the mayor of Athens, Haris Doukas, said.
“We are talking about an incredible disaster,” he said, adding that damage had occurred along the street the building was in, as well as behind it.
He said that two nearby buildings were left in a dangerous state, with inspections under way “to determine if they can remain standing or if they also have to be demolished”.
Some 30 rescuers and three sniffer dogs were at work at the site of the incident, Greece’s ANA news agency reported.
A specialised fire team investigating the cause of the blast was still at the scene, it said.

The residents had urged a fire drill to identify possible weaknesses in the emergency response plans for the district.

fb554cd611419cac: SEPTEMBER 26 — Benjamin Netanyahu went to the United Nations to explain why Israel is fighting on seven fronts, why its army is the most moral in the world, why its critics are cowards, and why the people walking out of the room are the real problem.
Then he held up a pager.
“Remember the beepers?” he asked, smiling like a man producing the rabbit at the end of a magic trick.
The trick, of course, was that the rabbit had been wired with explosives.

In September 2024, thousands of pagers and walkie-talkies exploded across Lebanon and Syria in an operation widely attributed to Israel. At least 37 people were killed and more than 3,000 injured. Children were among the dead. So were civilians. The blasts tore through homes, shops and streets. UN human-rights experts warned the attacks could constitute war crimes, including indiscriminate attacks. That is not a final court judgment. It is a warning that should have made any leader think twice before turning the device into a prop. Netanyahu looked at it and saw a punchline.
“Remember the beepers?”
Yes, Prime Minister. People remember the blood, too.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu holds up a pager while addressing the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York on September 24, 2026. — AFP pic

There is something grotesque about bringing a weapon associated with civilian deaths into the world’s diplomatic chamber and treating it like a championship belt. Imagine an accused arsonist arriving at a fire-safety conference, twirling the match and asking the audience if it remembers the flames. Imagine a pickpocket addressing a room of victims with, “Remember the wallets?” That isn’t wit. It’s a man so pleased with the performance that he has forgotten what the performance is about.

The United Nations is not a showroom for clever weapons. It is not a comedy club where the dead are the setup and the surviving families are expected to laugh at the punchline. It is supposed to be a place where leaders make the case for peace, or at least pretend to have read the menu.

No wonder delegates walked out. Netanyahu called them “moral cowards”. Perhaps it was easier than asking why so many chose the corridor over his speech. A walkout is not an argument, but neither is a pager held aloft like a party favour. Sometimes an empty chair is the most honest thing in the room.

His speech was a masterclass in changing the subject. Seven fronts. Seven enemies. Seven reasons the world should stop asking questions and start applauding. Israel, he said, was fighting everyone else’s fight. Hamas, Hezbollah, Iran, the Houthis, militias, terrorists: all packed into one vast, convenient silhouette called the enemy. Any Israeli action could then be placed beneath the same enormous umbrella labelled self-defence.

Hamas’s murder and kidnapping of Israeli civilians on October 7 was horrific. Israeli families deserve to grieve, and hostages deserved to come home. Saying so should not require a footnote. But grief is not a government’s lifetime licence to act without scrutiny. One atrocity does not turn every later decision into a moral blank cheque.

Netanyahu called criticism an “eighth front”, a war for truth. It is an elegant device: disagree with the government and you are no longer a critic; you are an enemy combatant in the information war. He said Israel sent millions of warnings to civilians. Those warnings matter. So do the dead, the displaced, the shattered neighbourhoods and the people who had nowhere safe to run. A leaflet is not a force field. A phone call telling a family to flee does not make the road out safe, or create a safe place at the other end.

Here is the arithmetic the speech cannot make disappear. Gaza’s Health Ministry reported 73,910 Palestinians killed by September 20, 2026. The total does not distinguish combatants from civilians. Unicef reported at least 21,700 children killed by June 30. And on September 24, after reviewing its records, the Committee to Protect Journalists documented 189 Palestinian journalists and media workers killed in Gaza. These figures have different cut-off dates and definitions; CPJ’s count does not mean every journalist was deliberately targeted. They are still numbers too large to hide behind a podium.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
A displaced Palestinian boy waits with others to receive hot meals distributed by a charity kitchen in Khan Yunis in the southern Gaza Strip on September 25, 2026. — AFP pic

Twenty-one thousand seven hundred children: say it slowly. These are not units in a briefing. They are names someone called at dinner. Shoes left by a door. A school uniform with no child left to wear it. One child dead is a family’s entire world ending. Multiply that by tens of thousands and you have not made the grief smaller. You have only made it harder to look at.

And the journalists? CPJ’s revised Gaza count is 189. That does not establish that everyone was targeted for their work; it does tell you how many reporters and media workers are no longer there to describe what they saw. When the people with cameras keep dying, and foreign journalists cannot freely enter Gaza, the world is left arguing over the pictures while the witnesses disappear. The facts need investigation. The journalists deserved protection. Their deaths should not be waved away as another hostile talking point.

Then there is NAZA, the documentary by Israeli filmmakers examining civilian deaths and Israeli military targeting in Gaza. The film wins an award at Venice; the government’s response is to threaten the filmmakers’ citizenship. Netanyahu says he wants laws that could strip citizenship from people who “smear” Israeli soldiers. Imagine the confidence required to claim your army has nothing to hide while threatening the people who made a film about what it does. If the filmmakers are wrong, answer them. Bring evidence. Make the case. A passport is not a rebuttal.

Defence Minister Israel Katz has been less subtle. He described the government’s language in Gaza and Lebanon as “evacuating the population, destroying the infrastructure and taking the territory.” He has also threatened to evacuate Gaza City’s million residents and destroy its buildings if one Israeli is kidnapped. There is no need to write a satirical version of that statement. The official version is already a black joke with the laughter removed.

Let’s be clear about what is being criticised here. This is not an indictment of Jews. Jewish people are not a single political bloc, and many Jews — including Israelis — criticise Netanyahu and oppose his government’s actions. Antisemitism is real and vicious; it must be confronted wherever it appears. But criticism of a government, its military conduct or the political ideology used to justify domination is not automatically hatred of Jews. Turn every criticism into antisemitism and the accusation becomes a shield for power instead of protection for people.

The Iran passage had its own curious little problem. Israel and the United States opened this latest round with strikes on Iran, described by Israel as “pre-emptive”, as Washington and Tehran were again negotiating over the nuclear dispute. Iran’s threats and actions do not vanish from the record. But if you strike first, then stand at the UN describing yourself as the civilisation-saving victim of aggression, you should expect a few people to check the timeline.

And the nuclear question: Israel is widely believed to possess nuclear weapons, though it officially confirms neither their existence nor its arsenal. The British House of Commons Library says Israel’s capability was developed outside the Non-Proliferation Treaty. Iran, for all the serious concerns about its nuclear programme, is a party to that treaty. The region’s only widely believed nuclear-armed state outside the NPT does not get to lecture its neighbours as if only their secrets count.

Britain has its own ghost in this room. The Balfour Declaration and the British Mandate helped shape the road to Israel’s creation; Britain did not create Israel single-handedly, but it played a pivotal and deeply contradictory role in Palestine’s fate. Now London objects, Netanyahu ignores it, and the former imperial midwife looks like a retired landlord arriving with a clipboard after the locks have been changed. The empire that helped write the prologue has discovered it no longer controls the plot.

That is the speech’s real spectacle: the man with the pager tells the world he is the only one brave enough to defend civilisation; the man threatening citizenship for filmmakers calls everyone else dishonest; the man whose country’s actions draw grave legal scrutiny insists the problem is the people asking questions.
The delegates walked out. Netanyahu called them cowards. He may prefer that story. It puts him at the centre, where he likes to stand, and turns the empty seats into props for his next scene.
But the pager remains. So do the dead. So do the children, the reporters, the families, the people beneath the rubble and the people still trying to tell their stories.
“Remember the beepers?” he asked.
We will remember the beepers.
We will also remember who held one up, who made it a joke, and who was missing from the punchline.

ad169ad015f9c0e4: Our resident Microsoft-watcher Richard Speed last week wrote about his seven-hour odyssey bringing a Windows 11 box up to snuff with the latest patches. I’ll see you that struggle, Richard, and raise you my experience updating a 2022-vintage Samsung Galaxy A33 Android smartphone. I spent about a year using the A33 as my daily driver and while it always did a job, the midrange machine is far from the speediest of smartphones and therefore a little frustrating to use. When a great deal for a premium handset came along I splashed some cash and shelved the A33 as a spare, safe in the knowledge that Samsung has promised to support it with new security updates until 2027. I store the A33 in the Basket Full Of Old Tech I Should Probably Have Thrown Out But Kept Just In Case, which sits on the floor of my home office – a room that gets no direct sunlight but is small, warm, and dry. All through the mild-if-clammy winter here in The Register’s Sydney, Australia, eyrie, the phone insisted it had moisture in its USB-C port and refused to charge. Because it’s a budget model, topping it up with wireless power isn’t an option. Spring has since sprung, so when the mercury topped 30°C (86°F) last weekend I left the phone in a warm and breezy spot for an afternoon. The phantom moisture evaporated, and before long I had the phone charged and running. Within seconds it suggested installing an OS update from April 2025, followed by six more – each of which required manual consent for download and install. The A33’s sluggishness soon manifested as an overlapping mess of updates in progress and reboots to finish installation of the last update. Every few minutes, the phone wanted me to approve or schedule a new download, or log back in. The phone is not so important to me that I needed to get all the updates installed ASAP. Two days of occasional attention at mealtimes and bedtime earned me a slow, old, but functional backup phone. My experience led me to concur with Mr Speed’s excellent argument that vendors need to ship better software so they’re less reliant on updates – and improve the process of updating devices. For Samsung that means rolling up past updates into cumulative downloads so leaving a device offline for a few months requires one intervention to modernize a device. The Korean giant could also do well to detect when a handset needs multiple updates and then inform users that its Smart Switch desktop app makes it possible to install cumulative updates in one fell swoop. ®

d4d7dcb8899f606e: KAJANG, Sept 26 — Madani Mart is opening master licensing applications to companies, investors, and strategic partners with financial and operational capabilities to accelerate its retail network expansion nationwide.

7db71001342ef57f: JOHANNESBURG, Sept 26 — South African police today found another body in Ekurhuleni, east of Johannesburg, bringing to 10 the number of women found dead in the municipality over the past two months.
The discovery adds to growing concern over violence against women in a country long plagued by violent crime, while police work to establish whether the killings are connected.

“At this stage, we can only confirm the discovery of the body. Crime scene management and all the necessary role players are currently on the scene,” police spokeswoman Brigadier Brenda Muridili said.

The nine other victims were mostly in their 20s and 30s, with some found stripped of their clothes and showing signs of sexual assault.
The first victim, a 37-year-old woman, was found naked and bound with cable ties on July 15. A suspect was arrested two days later.
Two other suspects, women aged 31 and 38, were arrested in connection with the ninth victim and charged on Monday.
Police have said that case may have stemmed from a relationship-related matter.
Gender-based violence is endemic in South Africa, despite years of government pledges to tackle the problem and the declaration of gender-based violence as a national disaster.

f068ceffb7836a37: MADRID, Sept 26 — A woman who was allegedly deceived into travelling to Pakistan and forced to marry a cousin has been rescued and returned to Spain, police said on Saturday.

The woman travelled to Pakistan in September 2025 after a relative allegedly told her that her family had dropped its opposition to her relationship with a Pakistani national who owns a computer shop in Barcelona.
Once there, however, relatives allegedly confiscated her Spanish passport, confined her to a family home and arranged her marriage to a cousin despite her opposition.
Her partner reported to police in April that she had been forcibly taken to Pakistan by members of her family.
He had previously been attacked with a bladed weapon in Barcelona by two men allegedly linked to the case.
Spanish police, working with Spain’s embassy in Pakistan, subsequently located the woman and organised her rescue and return to Spain.
She was given specialist support after returning, police said.
The investigation remained open while police worked to identify all those involved in the alleged forced marriage and the attack on her partner.

Barcelona has a sizeable Pakistani community, with more than 26,000 Pakistani nationals registered in the city, making it the third-largest foreign nationality group after Italians and Colombians. — AFP
b5be0a7e66ee0499: SINGAPORE, Sept 26 — Singapore’s government is reviewing property purchases made by officers involved in rail planning after a research paper found public servants appeared more likely than others to buy homes near future MRT stations before the locations were publicly announced.

The Public Service Division (PSD) said the review would cover purchases made between 2007 and 2011, the period highlighted in the paper, involving properties close to locations that were later announced as MRT stations, Singapore-based news outlet CNA reported today.

But the research, published earlier this month by the US-based National Bureau of Economic Research, has not been peer-reviewed and does not establish that individual civil servants committed misconduct.

The researchers said they found a higher incidence of property purchases near planned MRT stations by civil servants than by a comparable group, with the difference concentrated in the one to two years before station locations were publicly announced.

PSD said the statistical patterns were concerning, but did not by themselves establish whether any officer had access to non-public information about MRT station locations or whether such information influenced a property purchase.
“For example, information or speculation about planned MRT lines and stations may already be in the public domain or used to market new property developments,” PSD was quoted as saying last Friday.
The division said it would retrieve available records and examine the circumstances of individual transactions, noting that the purchases took place many years ago.
“If we find evidence that an officer used non-public information to make a property purchase for personal benefit, the case will be referred to the police for further investigation,” PSD said.

The paper estimated that, compared with its control group, civil servants made about 50 additional purchases of properties near future MRT stations two years before announcements and 63 additional purchases one year before.

The researchers put the gross value of those excess pre-announcement purchases at about S$138 million (RM431 million) and said the pattern was concentrated among mid-level officials and those working in agencies involved in MRT planning.

The study also reported similar patterns among people connected to the officials through shared residential addresses, although it used the term “relatives” for convenience and said this did not necessarily mean the individuals were family members.

PSD said Singapore’s public service has long had safeguards against officials using non-public information for personal benefit, including requirements to declare property purchases and controls over access to sensitive information.

It said the safeguards had been strengthened over time, with officers today required to declare and obtain approval before making personal transactions that could be affected by non-public information, including property, vehicles or financial instruments.

The paper, titled ‘Do Social Norms Substitute for Enforcement? Evidence from Public Officials’ Home Purchases in Singapore’, was authored by academics from Columbia University, Stanford University and the University of Hong Kong.

PSD said it had previously announced on September 14 that it was reviewing the paper’s data and methodology and would refer matters to the Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau if there was a material basis to do so.
Some Singapore academics acknowledged in the paper have since asked to have their names removed from the acknowledgements, according to local media reports.
PSD said conclusions of wrongdoing must ultimately be based on evidence and the facts of each case.

6e34eb69e7f7b5dc: SHAH ALAM, Sept 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today questioned the federal Opposition’s priorities, taking a swipe at its MPs for scrutinising his refusal to draw a prime ministerial salary while, he said, saying little about those who “sakau”, or steal, large sums of money.
Anwar recalled being questioned by Opposition MPs in Parliament over how he could support himself without taking his salary as prime minister.
He said he had also been told by the Opposition that even Prophet Muhammad received wages, but added that he had never heard that the Prophet took a salary.

“Then I said, I don’t take a salary, but I don’t fall under the B40 category. Firstly, I take the allowance,” he said during a gathering with Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) alumni and students at the university’s Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor.

He then questioned what the Opposition had chosen to focus on.
“But they want to ‘sibuk’ [interfere], want to be angry. Don’t take a salary, they’re angry. Those who ‘sakau’ [steal] a lot, they don’t mention,” he said, drawing laughter from the audience.
Anwar did not elaborate on whom he was referring to in his remarks about the Opposition.

Last month, Anwar also used the word “sakau” when speaking about alleged past financial mismanagement at Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), following the government’s July 29 release of a Royal Commission of Inquiry report into the pilgrims’ fund.

The RCI examined TH’s management and operations from 2014 to 2020. The government subsequently said investigations based on the report’s findings would proceed and that action would be taken if breaches of the law were established.
In 2024, PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang reportedly suggested in the Dewan Rakyat that Anwar was seeking to appear more pious than Prophet Muhammad by refusing to accept a salary.
Anwar has declined to draw his salaries as prime minister and finance minister since taking office in November 2022, while continuing to receive his allowance as Tambun MP.

1e641e6e91efe21b: MILAN, Sept 26 — Milan’s main international airport was officially renamed on Friday after former Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi, who died in 2023.
The airport is now called Aeroporto Milano-Malpensa Silvio Berlusconi, after the new name was approved in 2024 but faced legal challenges, German news agency dpa reported.

“Knowing that Milan-Malpensa Silvio Berlusconi Airport will welcome thousands of travellers from all over the world every day fills me with pride and emotion,” said Maria Elvira “Marina” Berlusconi, the late politician’s eldest daughter.
The airport is the second largest in Italy after Rome-Fiumicino.
Milan Mayor Giuseppe Sala stayed away from the renaming ceremony in protest, having previously opposed naming the airport after Berlusconi, who was born in the city.
“What was I supposed to do? Turn up with a forced smile?” he commented on Instagram.
Berlusconi was a deeply controversial figure both in Italy and abroad.
He served four terms as prime minister between 1994 and 2011, spending more than nine years in office — longer than any other Italian prime minister since the end of World War II.

His political career was marked by numerous legal fights, including a 2013 conviction for tax fraud and a trial over the so-called “bunga bunga” affair involving parties attended by some underage girls.
He was ultimately acquitted in that case.
Berlusconi’s Forza Italia party is now part of the three-party right-wing coalition led by Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s Brothers of Italy, which has governed Italy since 2022. — Bernama-dpa
69d26d290ee9b50f: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — A post-mortem has failed to establish the cause of death of a 14-year-old boy whose death is being investigated following allegations of bullying at a school hostel in Kuala Pilah, with police awaiting the results of further tests.

According to the MoD, the existing No. I Space Operations Squadron and No. II Space Warning Squadron give the RAF the ability to watch and warn of threats in space, but the latest unit will have the ability to act against those threats. This will be accomplished using “advanced technology,” we are told, including electronic warfare, to “disrupt, degrade and deny hostile actions.” In fact, the government says the UK has formally ruled out destructive anti-satellite missile testing, and instead continues to work through the UN Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space. We asked the MoD for further details on what the space force’s capabilities consist of, exactly, but a spokesperson told us there is not much more that can be said as the information is classified. The MoD states that satellites are critical for both national security and daily life, enabling intelligence gathering and missile warnings, while also providing telecoms and weather forecasts. The emergency services rely on satellite navigation systems for emergency responses, and energy networks use the same systems to organise power grids, making use of the precise time coding in such signals to synchronise operations. Last year, The Register reported that the MoD was working with the UK’s Space Agency on finding ways to protect orbiting satellites with technology that can spot when lasers are being used to try and dazzle them and disrupt communications. Four countries are known to have tested anti-satellite missiles; the US, Russia, China and India. The most recent incident was when Russia destroyed one of its own defunct orbiters in 2021, endangering the International Space Station. The ISS also had to conduct manoeuvres the same year to avoid space debris created by China blowing up one of its own satellites years earlier. In 2022, the United Nations passed a US-led resolution calling on countries to commit not to conduct any similar anti-satellite missile tests. That hasn’t stopped China, for one, looking at other ways of taking out orbital assets if it considers it necessary, looking at employing lasers and high-power microwaves to disable them. 1e588486cc3e4e18: A tired, simplistic narrative dominates Malaysian campaign stages and social media feeds: that Malay disunity is entirely DAP's fault.

While this rhetoric is highly effective at mobilising voters through fear, it is built on a shallow foundation. Blaming DAP is a convenient distraction, one that deliberately obscures the true root causes of the Malay political crisis.

The reality is that polarisation within the Malay community is not driven by an external threat. It is the direct result of internal dynamics, clashing egos and socioeconomic evolution. DAP did not fracture Malay politics; it has merely been weaponised as a bogeyman whenever the community's internal consensus begins to splinter.

Historically, every major rupture within the Malay political establishment has originated from internal power struggles, not external interference. The historic 1987 Umno crisis — a fierce showdown between Dr Mahathir Mohamad and Tengku Razaleigh Hamzah — birthed Semangat 46.
The 1998 Reformasi movement, sparked by Anwar Ibrahim's sacking from government, led to the creation of PKR. Decades later, the 1MDB scandal triggered the 2016 split that formed Bersatu.

All of these political earthquakes occurred deep within Umno's own backyard. They were driven by leadership conflicts and raw ambition, long before DAP was ever accepted into mainstream ruling coalitions.

Furthermore, the Malay electorate is not, and has never been, a monolith. Even before independence, Malay political thought was fractured into distinct ideological factions. Malay nationalism, anchored by Umno, focused on ethnic privileges and the social contract.
Conversely, Islamic politics, championed by PAS, demanded a state rooted in religious law — a doctrinal divergence that triggered their split from Umno as early as 1951.

Today, progressive movements like PKR and Amanah contest this space by championing institutional reform and social justice within a pluralistic framework, alongside a constantly shifting constellation of splinter parties.

With segments of the electorate prioritising economic integrity, others focusing on religious identity, and some remaining loyal to traditional structures, a fragmented political landscape is inevitable.
Where, then, does DAP fit into this theatre?

The party has become a convenient rhetorical shield. When multiple Malay-based parties are forced to fish from the exact same voter pool, they inevitably fall into a hyper-nationalistic contest to prove who is "more Malay" or "more Islamic".

In this arena, the fastest way to destroy an opponent’s credibility is to label them a "puppet" or "agent" of DAP. This strategy shifts the focus away from a party's own policy failures by exploiting historical trauma and racial anxieties for short-term electoral gain.
Ultimately, a diversification of political choices is a hallmark of a maturing democracy, not a crisis to be feared. It is time for Malay political leaders to stop pointing fingers outwardly.

Blaming DAP will not reunite the community. The real challenge lies in the leadership’s inability to forge a consensus, manage ideological differences with maturity, and prioritise national stability over personal agendas.
Until they look in the mirror, they will continue fighting external shadows.
Moaz Nair is an FMT reader.
